## Compact Rules

Pre-digested rules per skill. Delegators copy matching blocks into sub-agent prompts as `## Project Standards (auto-resolved)`.

### branch-pr

- Every PR MUST link an approved issue (must have `status:approved` label)
- Every PR MUST have exactly one `type:*` label
- Branch naming: `^(feat|fix|chore|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|revert)\/[a-z0-9._-]+$`
- PR body must include: Closes/Fixes/Resolves #N, type checkbox, summary bullet, changes table, test plan, contributor checklist
- Automated checks pass before merge: issue reference, status:approved, type label, shellcheck
- Conventional commits: `type(scope)!: description` — no `Co-Authored-By` trailers
- Blank PRs blocked without issue linkage

### chained-pr

- Split PRs over 400 changed lines unless maintainer accepts `size:exception`
- Keep each PR reviewable in ≤60 minutes
- Use one deliverable work unit per PR; tests/docs with the unit they verify
- State start, end, dependencies, follow-up, and out-of-scope in every chained PR
- Every child PR includes a dependency diagram marking current with `📍`
- Feature Branch Chain: draft tracker PR, children target parent branch
- Stacked PRs: each slice lands independently to main
- Verify each PR independently: CI, tests, docs, rollback scope, clean diff
- Never mix chain strategies after user chooses one

### cognitive-doc-design

- Lead with the answer: decision, action, or outcome first; context after
- Progressive disclosure: happy path first, then details, edge cases, references
- Chunk: group related info in small sections; keep flat lists short
- Signpost: headings, labels, callouts, summaries so readers navigate easily
- Recognition over recall: tables, checklists, examples, templates over prose
- Review empathy: design so reviewers verify intent without reconstructing the whole story
- PR docs: state what to review first, what is out of scope, link prev/next PR

### comment-writer

- Start with the actionable point — no recap before feedback
- Sound like a thoughtful teammate, not a corporate bot
- Prefer 1-3 short paragraphs or a tight bullet list
- Explain WHY when asking for a change (technical reason)
- Comment on highest-value issue, not every tiny preference
- Match thread language — Spanish threads use Rioplatense voseo (podés, tenés, fijate)
- No em dashes — use commas, periods, or parentheses
- Format: `<observation/request>`, `<why it matters (optional)>`, `<next action>`

### go-testing

- Prefer table-driven tests with `t.Run(tt.name, ...)`
- Test behavior and state transitions, not implementation trivia
- Use `t.TempDir()` for filesystem tests
- Integration tests skippable with `testing.Short()` for external commands
- Bubbletea: test `Model.Update()` directly; use `teatest` only for interactive flows
- Golden files: deterministic, update through `-update` path, rerun without `-update`
- Small mocks/interfaces around system/command boundaries

### issue-creation

- Blank issues disabled — MUST use template (bug_report.yml or feature_request.yml)
- Every issue gets `status:needs-review` on creation
- Maintainer must add `status:approved` before any PR can be opened
- Questions go to Discussions, not issues
- Bug report: pre-flight checks, description, steps to reproduce, expected/actual behavior, OS, agent, shell
- Feature request: pre-flight checks, problem description, proposed solution, affected area
- Labels: bug+status:needs-review (bug report), enhancement+status:needs-review (feature request)

### judgment-day

- Launch two blind judges in parallel with identical target and criteria; never review code yourself
- Wait for both judges before synthesis; never accept partial verdict
- Classify warnings: `WARNING (real)` only if normal intended use triggers it; else downgrade to `INFO`
- Ask before fixing Round 1 confirmed issues
- After fix agent runs, re-launch both judges in parallel before commit/push/done
- Terminal states: `JUDGMENT: APPROVED` or `JUDGMENT: ESCALATED`
- After 2 fix iterations with remaining issues, ask user whether to continue
- Resolve project skills before launching agents (read skill registry)

### skill-creator

- `description` MUST be one physical line, quoted, YAML-safe, ≤250 chars, trigger words first
- Frontmatter: `name`, `description`, `license`, `metadata.author`, `metadata.version`
- Body sections: Activation Contract, Hard Rules, Decision Gates, Execution Steps, Output Contract, References
- Target 180–450 tokens body; move detail to `assets/` or `references/`
- No `Keywords` section; preserve trigger words in `description`
- References must point to local files
- Use imperative instructions, not tutorials or background prose

### work-unit-commits

- Commit by deliverable work unit: behavior, fix, migration, or docs — not by file type
- Keep tests with the code they verify in the same commit
- Keep docs with the user-visible change they explain
- Each commit tells a story — reviewer understands why it exists from diff + message
- Each commit should be a candidate chained PR when the change grows
- Before commit: one clear purpose, repo makes sense after this commit, rollback is reasonable
- If SDD tasks forecast >400 lines, group commits into chained PR slices before implementation
- Commit message explains outcome, not file list

### imagegen

- Default to built-in `image_gen` tool for raster images; CLI fallback only if user explicitly asks
- For transparent images: use built-in with chroma-key + local removal script; ask before CLI `gpt-image-1.5`
- Never silently switch from built-in or CLI gpt-image-2 to CLI gpt-image-1.5 — ask first
- Save project-bound assets to workspace; never leave only at default `$CODEX_HOME/*` path
- For edits, preserve invariants aggressively and save non-destructively
- Use distinct built-in calls per distinct asset; CLI `generate-batch` only when user chose CLI mode
- Prompt augmentation: normalize detailed prompts, add tasteful detail to generic ones, never add extra subjects
- Structured prompt spec: use case slug, asset type, scene, subject, style, composition, lighting, constraints
- Do not overwrite existing assets — create versioned sibling filenames

### openai-docs

- For Codex self-knowledge: run the Codex manual fetch helper first, then Docs MCP, then official-domain web fallback
- For non-Codex OpenAI docs: use `mcp__openaiDeveloperDocs__search_openai_docs` + `fetch_openai_doc` before web fallback
- For model selection: fetch `latest-model.md` first; for upgrades run `resolve-latest-model-info.js` only for unversioned targets
- Preserve explicit target model requests even if a newer model exists — mention newer as optional only
- Keep migration changes narrow and behavior-preserving; leave history/docs/fixtures unchanged unless asked
- For API reference/schema: use `get_openapi_spec` when available
- If MCP tools fail: install server yourself before asking user; use official domain web search as last resort
- Treat manual and Docs MCP as separate lanes, not interchangeable

### plugin-creator

- Plugin name: lower-case hyphen-case, ≤64 chars, normalized from user input
- Always creates `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` with validated manifest; no `[TODO: ...]` placeholders
- Default to personal marketplace (`~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`); repo/team marketplace opt-in only
- Marketplace entry must include: `policy.installation`, `policy.authentication`, `category`
- Default policy: `installation: AVAILABLE`, `authentication: ON_INSTALL`
- For existing plugin updates: use `update_plugin_cachebuster.py`, never hand-edit marketplace files
- Run `validate_plugin.py` before handing back
- Do not tell user to run `codex plugin marketplace add` for default personal marketplace path

### skill-installer

- Default install source: `https://github.com/openai/skills/tree/main/skills/.curated`
- Experimental skills: `--path skills/.experimental`
- Use helper scripts: `list-skills.py`, `install-skill-from-github.py`
- Install uses direct download first; falls back to git sparse checkout on auth failure
- Aborts if destination skill directory already exists
- Installs into `$CODEX_HOME/skills/<skill-name>` (defaults to `~/.codex/skills`)
- Private repos work via existing git credentials or `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN`
- After install, tell user: "Restart Codex to pick up new skills."

## Loading protocol

1. Match task context and target files against the `Trigger` column.
2. Copy matching compact rules from the `## Compact Rules` section into the sub-agent prompt as `## Project Standards (auto-resolved)`.
3. If only path-based resolution is needed, pass matching `Path` values to the sub-agent under `## Skills to load before work`.
4. If no matching skill exists, proceed without project skill injection and report `skill_resolution: none`.
